text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- King Hussein says he is concerned with the Turkish presence in northern Iraq and stresses Jordan's support for Iraq's territorial unity.
- The government plans to launch a major programme to help define land uses.
- Opposition parties condemn the Turkish attack on northern Iraq.
- King Hussein accepts the resignation of Ahmed al-Lawzi, appointed speaker of the Senate (the upper house of parliament), on health grounds.
- Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat due in Amman on Sunday to hold talks with King Hussein on latest developments in Middle East peace.
- Crown Prince Hassan says the social safety network plan to help ease poverty and unemployment is for all Jordanians and has no "political objectives."
- King Hussein says "now is the time to be committed to the principles of peace, and democracy does not mean overstepping freedoms and attacking rights of others."

- Part of the defence team in the trial of the Jordanian soldier charged with shooting dead seven Israeli schoolgirls withdraws from case because of the insistence of the prosecution to summon Israeli witnesses to testify in court.

- Jordanian-U.S talks are expected to result in an extra $100 million aid allocation to the kingdom; a top level Jordanian delegation headed by Deputy Prime Minister Anani in ongoing talks in Washington on how to attract U.S. investments.
- King condemns all attempts to redraw regional map.
